definitions.rationale: Macro equation defining the named factorizeStep statement block used by the proof model.
definitions.text:
rule factorizeStep
    => If(
         Compare(BinOp("%", Name("n"), Name("divisor")),
                 CmpOp("==", Int(0))),
         Expr(Call(Attribute(Name("factors"), "append"), Name("divisor")))
         Assign(Name("n"), BinOp("//", Name("n"), Name("divisor"))),
         AugAssign(Name("divisor"), "+", Int(1)))

definitions.rationale: Macro equation defining the named factorizeBody statement sequence.
definitions.text:
rule factorizeBody
    => Assign(Name("factors"), ListExpr(.Exprs))
       Assign(Name("divisor"), Int(2))
       While(Compare(Name("n"), CmpOp(">", Int(1))), factorizeStep)
       Return(Name("factors"))

definitions.rationale: Macro equation defining factorizeDef as the target function definition.
Base equation of the factorLoop mathematical summary recurrence.
definitions.text:
rule factorLoop(N:Int, _D:Int, VS:ValSeq) => VS
    requires N <=Int 1

definitions.rationale: Divisible-case equation of the factorLoop mathematical summary recurrence.
definitions.text:
rule factorLoop(N:Int, D:Int, VS:ValSeq)
    => factorLoop((N -Int pyMod(N, D)) /Int D, D,
                  valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(D, .ValSeq)))
    requires N >Int 1 andBool D >Int 0
         andBool pyMod(N, D) ==Int 0

definitions.rationale: Nondivisible-case equation of the factorLoop mathematical summary recurrence.
definitions.text:
rule factorLoop(N:Int, D:Int, VS:ValSeq)
    => factorLoop(N, D +Int 1, VS)
    requires N >Int 1 andBool D >Int 0
         andBool pyMod(N, D) =/=Int 0

definitions.rationale: Equation defining primeFactors by initializing factorLoop with divisor 2 and an empty accumulator.
Base equation of the factorDivisor proof-summary recurrence.
definitions.text:
rule factorDivisor(N:Int, D:Int) => D
    requires N <=Int 1

definitions.rationale: Divisible-case equation of the factorDivisor proof-summary recurrence.
definitions.text:
rule factorDivisor(N:Int, D:Int)
    => factorDivisor((N -Int pyMod(N, D)) /Int D, D)
    requires N >Int 1 andBool D >Int 0
         andBool pyMod(N, D) ==Int 0

definitions.rationale: Nondivisible-case equation of the factorDivisor proof-summary recurrence.
definitions.text:
rule factorDivisor(N:Int, D:Int)
    => factorDivisor(N, D +Int 1)
    requires N >Int 1 andBool D >Int 0
         andBool pyMod(N, D) =/=Int 0

proved_derived_lemmas.rationale: Its configuration rewrite and precondition exactly match the factorize-loop claim, which prove.sh first proves against FACTORIZE-VERIFICATION before compiling this rule in FACTORIZE-VERIFICATION-WITH-LOOP-LEMMA.
proved_derived_lemmas.text:
rule
    <k>
      #while(Compare(Name("n"), CmpOp(">", Int(1))), factorizeStep)
      ~> KONT
      => KONT
    </k>
    <env> L </env>
    <scopes>
      (L |-> scope(
        ("n" |-> N
         "divisor" |-> D
         "factors" |-> ref(H)),
        parent(0)))
      SC
      =>
      (L |-> scope(
        ("n" |-> 1
         "divisor" |-> factorDivisor(N, D)
         "factors" |-> ref(H)),
        parent(0)))
      SC
    </scopes>
    <heap>
      (H |-> list(VS)) HP
      => (H |-> list(factorLoop(N, D, VS))) HP
    </heap>
    requires N >=Int 1 andBool D >=Int 2
    [priority(40), label(factorize-loop-lemma)]
